insight: Before implementing ANY host-specific feature (hooks, MCP, task graph, model routing, UI paradigms, Background Tasks), invoke the 'research' skill to verify current host documentation. Training data on host APIs is often stale by months. Assuming 'Claude Code only supports 3 hook events' when docs show 28 led to under-implementation of 25 hooks and wrong documentation in FRAMEWORK-STATE.md and proposals.

Stored knowledge in references/knowledge/ decays silently as upstream docs evolve. At session 2026-04-24, stored knowledge said Codex had no native hooks (WRONG — 6 events), Gemini hooks were unsupported (WRONG — 11 events), Kimi had 11 events (WRONG — 13), and Claude had 27 events (WRONG — 28). Before acting on a knowledge file's claim about a host capability, WebFetch the upstream doc to verify. Add a 'last_verified' field to CAPABILITIES.md frontmatter and refuse to use knowledge >30 days old for host wiring decisions.

All four svc host CLIs (Claude Code, Kimi, Codex, Gemini) pass hook payloads as JSON on stdin. Scripts wired with `node hook.mjs "$TOOL_INPUT"` break because $TOOL_INPUT is never populated — argv gets literal `$TOOL_INPUT` string or empty. Every call then fingerprints to hash({}) and stateful hooks (loop-guard) block after N unrelated calls. Rule: always read stdin first, argv fallback is only for legacy compat. Shared helper at hooks/lib/hook-payload.mjs.

The universal hard-block exit code across all four svc host CLIs is exit 2 (stderr contains reason, action aborted). Exit 1 is NOT a documented contract for any host. Exit 0 + JSON `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision:"deny"` is the modern soft-decision path. When a hook must hard-abort and the reason is sufficient, prefer `blockViaExit(reason)` which writes to stderr and exits 2.

Framework self-improvement must follow plan-changeset discipline when the change carries semantic risk, independent of size. Three risk signals trigger: (1) contract change — function signature / hook wire protocol / frontmatter schema / config format / CLI args; (2) hot-path edit — hooks/svc-*, hooks/lib/*, scripts/wire-*, tier-1 validators; (3) refactor without behavior change — .js↔.mjs port, module extraction, renames of frequently-referenced exports. Exempt: purely additive new files, documentation-only edits, learning updates, proposal lifecycle moves. Supersedes the older size-based rule (>2 files or >50 lines) which mis-targeted: it gated harmless additive work and let small-but-risky edits sail through. Full rule at rules/plan-changeset-trigger.md.

Tests that depend on persistent counter files or shared session state are flaky across runs. Always use unique session IDs per test run, or explicitly reset/clean shared state in test setup/teardown. The completion-guard counter at /tmp/svc-completion-guard/<session_id> caused test 7 to fail non-deterministically.
last_applied: 2026-06-10 WI-399 run2: drove the session+cwd counter keying in svc-task-completion-guard (3 fixture validators went hermetic)

insight: When BASH_XTRACEFD is set to a custom file descriptor and script(1) is used to create a pseudo-TTY, the inner shell inherits the fd redirect. This can cause stdout to be silently redirected to /dev/null. Always unset BASH_XTRACEFD before calling script(1) in test scripts that use exec N>/dev/null + set -x.

G5 self-review MUST execute every tier-1 script, not just the newly-added regression test. WI-072 port broke validate-claude-hook-e2e and validate-kimi-hook-e2e (both calling the renamed svc-workflow-guard.js) and validate-framework-self-management (asserting a hooks.json string I changed). The new regression test (validate-workflow-guard.sh) passed in isolation and hid all three failures. Rule: in review-gate step of plan-changeset, `bash test-framework/evals/run-all-evals.sh --tier1` before declaring G5 PASS. Takes ~30s. Not optional.

Framework-lane WIs can silently skip mandatory lane skills (e.g. improve-framework between evolve-framework and write-spec) when the user's execution prompt enumerates skills in a different order. Reviewers do not catch this under standard scope-lock because they grade document content not process shape. Fix: lane-tasks JSON must carry 'upstream_completed' + 'upstream_skipped_with_justification' fields; plan-changeset and execute-changeset refuse to proceed if the fields are missing or incomplete; tier-1 validate-lane-upstream-completeness enforces mechanically; review-plan prompts gain a lane-compliance focus item that explicitly asks: 'For the declared lane, list every mandatory upstream skill. Is each either completed (cite artifact) or skipped (cite pipeline-decisions.jsonl justification)?'

Adversarial plan reviewers (Kimi + Codex) go off-script when given scope-lock prompts: they spend their turn reading files, running shell commands, and writing artifacts instead of producing YAML findings. Kimi attempted to create capture-idea/references/ files during WI-073 review. Codex ran 6 exec commands against skills-manifest/routing-rules/plan-changeset-trigger during WI-074 and never emitted findings. Fix: reviewer scripts prepend an OUTPUT-FIRST preamble ('emit YAML findings block first, explore AFTER'), enforce read-only sandbox, tail-parse output and exit 2 if findings block absent. Learning locked via tier-1 validate-review-plan-readonly.sh.

Scope-lock reviewer contracts restrict evaluation to document content. This blocks reviewers from catching process-shape errors like skipped lane skills (e.g., WI-073 skipped improve-framework between evolve-framework and write-spec; no reviewer flagged it). Fix: add explicit 'lane compliance' focus dimension (g) to both reviewer prompts: reviewer must list every mandatory upstream skill and verify each is completed (cite artifact) or skipped-with-justification (cite pipeline-decisions.jsonl). Unnamed lane skill = REJECT. Dimension added to references/plan-review-protocol.md as canonical rubric.

Framework reviews must be reproducible across machines. Before this learning, codex exec inherited the user's ~/.codex/config.toml model setting — a developer with a weaker local default would get a lower-quality review without knowing. Fix: reviewer scripts pin model + reasoning_effort via -c flags. Already applied to review-plan-codex.sh (gpt-5.5 + high). Principle: every external-tool invocation in tier-1 or review infrastructure must have reproducibility-relevant config pinned inline, not inherited from user config.

capture-idea/scripts/parse-proposal.mjs extractBlocks() flushes the current block on ANY heading regardless of depth. For monolithic proposals with subsection headings (### US-XX) under a top-level block (## Acceptance Criteria), the sub-heading triggers flush before the US content accumulates, resulting in empty AC block. Similarly `## Goal` vs `## Goals` both map to the same 'goals' key but renderWi() treats leaf.goal and blocks.goals as separate fields, producing TBD in one of them. Fix: extractBlocks should only flush on headings at depth ≤ the current block's starting depth; deeper sub-headings are content. And collapse 'goal' + 'goals' in BLOCK_NAMES to a single key with leaf.goal derived from the heading text only for leaf mode. First observed during WI-074 emission — WI-074 needed manual Goal + AC fill-in after promotion.

scripts/wire-hooks.mjs isAlreadyWired() check had gaps — hooks whose hookId lacked an explicit case in the switch always returned false, so every setup re-run appended a new copy. svc-loop-guard accumulated 37 duplicates across sessions; other hooks similar. Fix: generic post-merge dedup pass keyed on (matcher, sorted(commands)). Safety net regardless of isAlreadyWired completeness. Enforced via tier-1 validate-settings-no-duplicate-hooks.sh which runs the script twice on a scratch settings.json and asserts output is identical.

scripts/wire-hooks.mjs hard-coded RENAMED_FILES list with a single entry (svc-workflow-guard.js→.mjs from WI-072). Any future .js→.mjs port would silently break installs that still had old paths. Fix: move to hooks/.renames.json registry (single source of truth). Script reads it on every invocation; missing registry falls back to hard-coded list for robustness during fresh clones.

evolve-framework and improve-framework produce DIFFERENT artifact types. Conflating them — e.g., embedding per-leaf fix briefs in an evolution proposal — causes downstream WIs to skip improve-framework entirely (observed WI-073). Rule: evolution proposals survey N gaps (no fix briefs); improvement proposals carry exactly one gap's fix brief. When a gap merits a fix brief, extract it from the evolution proposal into its own framework-improvement-<name>.md before promoting to a WI. Both skill docs now carry a reciprocal 'Scope boundary' section naming the other.

Adding a rule file to rules/ without a matching skills-manifest.json rulesRegistry entry is a silent bookkeeping gap — scripts/lint-skills-manifest.mjs fails at an unrelated WI time (observed WI-072 where plan-changeset-trigger.md was unregistered). Fix: tier-1 validator validate-rules-registry-completeness.sh does bidirectional check between rules/ directory and rulesRegistry entries. Catches drift early, near the commit that introduced it.

Deleting a git worktree that ~/.claude/skills/ symlinks pointed into leaves all those symlinks dangling. Claude Code still loads settings.json with the old paths at session start, so hooks fail at next invocation. Observed 3× during 2026-04-24 framework session after WI-073/074/075 closeouts. Fix: tier-1 validate-claude-skills-symlinks.sh detects dead symlinks and instructs ./setup --host claude as recovery. Does NOT auto-run setup (out of scope for detector); agents that see this validator fail should run setup themselves before proceeding.

summary: setup creates rule symlinks from current rulesRegistry entries but never prunes old ones. When a rule is renamed/removed from the registry, the symlink is orphaned — WI-079's validator catches it after the fact but it should never have persisted. Fix: setup walks $SKILLS_TARGET/rules and $RULES_DIR after the registry loop, removes symlinks whose targets don't exist, preserves symlinks pointing outside $SCRIPT_DIR (foreign framework installs). Complements WI-079 (detection) with WI-080 (self-healing). Reports 'Rules:  pruned N orphan symlink(s)' when non-zero.

capture-idea --from-proposal's self-exclusion rule matches on Source anchor but fails when the proposal is moved proposals/ → proposals/done/ AFTER the original WI was authored. A parallel session captured 2026-04-24-framework-improvement-symlink-refresh-after-worktree.md from done/ and emitted WI-081, duplicating already-merged WI-079. Fix direction: self-exclusion should also check the proposal's basename (not just path) against closed WIs' Source frontmatter, OR consult DONE.md / the merged-pr field in lane-tasks-*.json. Until patched, reviewers should spot duplicates by scanning WI subject against DONE.md before spending cycles.

insight: `opencode models` only lists what the user's ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json defines — it is not a vendor registry. When a new MiMo model drops (e.g., V2.5 on 2026-04-22), wiring is a config edit, not a wait. Rule: to wire a new MiMo/OpenAI-compatible model, (1) add entry under provider.mimo.models in opencode.json, (2) mirror in references/opencode-mimo-config.json, (3) add harnesses.mimo.models.<id> in references/model-registry.json with invocation `opencode run --model mimo/<id>`, (4) update svc-default profile label mapping, (5) verify via `bash scripts/resolve-model.sh EXEC --json`. Initial (wrong) instinct was to defer until `opencode models` showed the new ID — that list is downstream of our own config.

capture-idea --from-proposal's extractBlocks originally flushed the current block on ANY heading. When a proposal nested `### US-XX` subheadings under `## Acceptance Criteria` (common pattern for multi-user-story proposals), the `### US-01` heading triggered a flush before any content was appended, losing the entire AC block. Observed on 3 of 7 April 24 framework proposals (reviewer-safety, skip-conditions-registry, wire-hooks-hygiene). Second bug in the same render path: `## Goal` renders TBD for monolithic proposals because renderWi reads heading-derived leaf.goal (empty) instead of blocks.goals (populated). Fix (WI-100): extractBlocks only flushes on headings matching a BLOCK_NAMES key; unknown headings become block content. renderWi prefers blocks.goals over leaf.goal and drops the redundant `## Goals` section. Regression fixture: capture-idea/references/tests/fixture-nested-us-headings.md.

Parallel capture-idea sessions collided on WI numbers pre-WI-098 (observed 079/080/081 renumbering during a single day). Fix: POSIX-atomic reservation via fs.writeFileSync(path, '', {flag:'wx'}) which throws EEXIST if another process already created that WI-NNN.md. Loop: start from nextWiNumber(), try create, on EEXIST bump N+1 and retry. No separate lock file needed. Scope: emit-wis.mjs (--from-proposal mode) ships with this protection; intake mode still needs same treatment (follow-up). Dry-run skips reservation to avoid polluting the WI dir on inspection.

capture-idea --from-proposal self-exclusion missed duplicates when a proposal was moved proposals/→done/ after merge. Root cause: monolithic proposals render Source as a bare path (no § anchor), but findExistingWiByAnchor only matched on anchor. Fix (WI-101): extend to findExistingWiByAnchorOrBasename and fall back to basename-match only for monolithic proposals (for phased, sibling leaves share basename so basename-only would false-skip). Companion to WI-098 (atomic allocation) — together they close the parallel-session duplicate-WI failure surface. Previous learning 'capture-idea-self-exclusion-misses-post-merge-proposal-move' conf 8 is now prevention-landed; bump to 9.

Premature-completion failure mode (WIs marked done but with inconsistent close-out artifacts) observed across ≥5 past WIs. Fix (WI-095 v1): scripts/verify-wi-closeout.mjs audits every DONE.md entry for (a) Status VERIFIED in WI-NNN.md, (b) DONE.md row present, (c) INDEX.md row shows status:verified, (d) git log on main references WI-NNN. Tier-1 validator validate-wi-closeout-evidence.sh runs this audit on every sweep. Override path: WI frontmatter '**Close-Override:** <reason>' line. Product-lane extension (prod-URL Playwright, bundle-hash) deferred until WI-097 wrapper lands to avoid token regression.

≥6 sessions stalled mid-execution when a prerequisite file was missing or Write was sandbox-blocked. Fix (WI-096 v1): scripts/preflight.mjs accepts a JSON payload (skill/inputs/outputs), checks inputs exist+readable and outputs have writable parent dirs, exits 1 with a JSON diagnostic on failure. Pattern doc at references/preflight-pattern.md. Advisory tier-1 validator validate-preflight-coverage.sh reports coverage but does not block — rollout is incremental. Once coverage reaches 100%, flip the validator to blocking.

Raw Playwright MCP tools (browser_snapshot, browser_click, etc.) return page-sized payloads. Returning them to the parent orchestrator burns context faster than any other framework action — a single browser_snapshot can be 5-20K tokens. Fix (WI-097 doctrine v1): (a) never hand browser-verify to the user; (b) never return raw MCP output to parent; (c) go through a compact wrapper that returns only verdict-shape JSON; (d) evidence files live on disk, paths only in stdout. Wrapper does not yet exist in svc — filed as WI-102 as prerequisite for full enforcement. Doctrine doc: references/browser-verify-doctrine.md.

In the research skill (post-WI-090), the agent MUST dispatch to gemini-cli as PRIMARY. Falling back to in-session Claude WebSearch is only legitimate when gemini-cli has actually failed (errored / timed out / returned partial). Choosing Claude up-front because 'WebSearch is more reliable' or 'we want to preserve gemini quota' is a self-inflicted rationalization — Claude tokens cost real $ on the parent's Max bill while gemini-cli runs free or against an already-paid Pro subscription. The pre-scope artifact's 'sub_agent_selection' justification must name a CONCRETE failure mode of gemini-cli for this run, not a hypothetical or a quota-preservation argument. Reviewer hook: any pre-scope where sub_agent_selection=claude without 'gemini-cli failed' or 'gemini-cli unavailable' or env override SVC_RESEARCH_AGENT=claude is a HIGH-severity finding. Source: 2026-04-25 session — agent invoked /research for google-ai-pro extraction, picked Claude up-front citing 'preserve gemini quota', burned ~30K parent context tokens on a task gemini-cli would have done free. Fix landed: rules/research-must-use-gemini-cli.md + tier-1 validator that scans pre-scope artifacts for the violation pattern.

The Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan (200M credits/mo, accessed via token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1) is RESTRICTED TO DEVELOPER TOOLING per ToS. Authorized: IDE coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, OpenCode), personal exploration. Forbidden: production app backends, automated scripts outside an IDE, customer-facing AI features, batch jobs against the token-plan URL. Routing production traffic = ToS violation, account suspension risk. Default throughput limits (100 RPM / 10M TPM = ~1.67 RPS) would 429 production loads anyway. For production use of MiMo models, register on the MiMo Open Platform with Business Verification and use Pay-As-You-Go (~$0.40/$2.00 per Mtok input/output, MiMo-V2.5). Source verified 2026-04-25 via gemini-cli research against official MiMo ToS + business-verification page + xiaomimimo.com pricing pages. PREVIOUSLY claimed in registry that the 200M Token Plan pool could 'cover all Example Marketplace AI volume for free' — that was wrong. Capability-concierge / ship-lens / migration-cost analyses must NOT treat Token Plan as a production AI budget. svc-default profile use of mimo-v2.5 for EXEC delegation IS within ToS because it routes through opencode (a developer/coding tool).

When acting on a multi-phase proposal, audit whether later phases are already satisfied (possibly under a different name/structure) BEFORE planning or executing them. The reinvention-detection rule (proposals/2026-04-26-reinvention-detection-existing-infra-check.md, merged as PR #42) was filed to catch "recommending NEW infra when project already has equivalent" for external systems — but the same failure mode applies to proposal phases authored months earlier. Specifically observed 2026-04-26 in WI-127: I uncritically accepted the proposals/2026-04-26-drop-flows-claude-host-uses-skills-only.md mental model that Phase 2 needed parallel hooks/{claude,codex,gemini}/ directories. The actual repo had already shipped a different (better) parity model: shared host-neutral hooks/svc-*.mjs + per-host wire scripts (wire-hooks.mjs, wire-codex-hooks.mjs, wire-gemini-hooks.mjs). I should have run `ls hooks/` and re-read proposals/2026-04-24-four-host-hook-parity.md FIRST. The user called it: "why didn't you find that earlier if you follow framework?" Fix: before planning any deferred phase from a proposal, run a phase-status audit against current repo state — list phase outputs the proposal predicts and grep/ls for evidence each one already exists (or not).

codex CLI (OpenAI) exposes a working internal generate_image tool through `codex exec` that produces ~1672x941 photoreal PNGs in ~90s. Auth uses ChatGPT-Plus/Pro id_token (not OPENAI_API_KEY which is None for sub users). Single-prompt-single-image is reliable; multi-image prompts timeout. Output lands in ~/.codex/generated_images/<session>/ then is cp'd to repo. This is the working image-gen route for builders with ChatGPT-sub but no OpenAI API key, no Vertex AI, no Imagen scope. Sourced: Example Marketplace WI-116 landing iter2 photoreal hero — gemini CLI/OAuth/Vertex all returned 403/scope-insufficient/no-tool; codex worked first-try.

The OAuth token in ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json (acquired via `gemini auth login`) does NOT include scope for generativelanguage.googleapis.com image-gen models (gemini-2.5-flash-image, imagen-*). Returns 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT. Imagen 4 via aiplatform.googleapis.com also 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on consumer project. Conclusion: programmatic Gemini image-gen requires either (a) explicit AI Studio API key or (b) a paid Google Cloud project with Vertex AI billing — Gemini-app subscription alone (Pro/Ultra) does NOT grant API image-gen. Use codex CLI or Imagen-with-API-key instead.

The documented Base44 'BuildCanary coding/write unstuck' (CLAUDE.md WI-087 pattern) can ITSELF fail with the same non-fast-forward error it was designed to fix. Symptom: github/sync returns already_up_to_date:true with stale last_git_commit_hash mismatch (sandbox at COMMIT_A, main at COMMIT_B>A); coding/write to pages/BuildCanary errors with 'git push origin main rejected non-fast-forward' regardless of content; deploy serves stale bundle indefinitely. Observed 2026-04-26 during Example Marketplace WI-117 deploy after multiple successful syncs in same session. Workaround: only known escape is human-open Base44 dashboard UI tab to fire auto-detect rebuild. Programmatic recovery from headless agent session is currently impossible. Fix-direction for svc base44-environment skill: add escalation step that (a) detects this specific signature: needs_to_add_diff:true + last_git_commit_hash<origin + non-fast-forward error on coding/write, (b) surfaces to user with explicit 'open Base44 UI now' message rather than retry-loop.

In multi-tenant apps where the context provider defaults currentScope to entities.X.filter({owner_id})[0], test seeds at a hardcoded scope (named seed location, fixed workspace) become invisible if accumulated test data shifted what allLocations[0] resolves to. Tests must seed at the app-default scope OR drive the UI to the seed scope through a disambiguated control. Mixing the two fails silently — UI looks fine, stats just stay 0. Pattern observed in Example Marketplace WI-132 (J04 stat tests, 14 accumulated locations on stream-B owner).

Test helpers that resolve 'owned X' / 'scoped X' must use the SAME filter query the app uses. Helpers using list() + permissive ownership checks (email-fallback, created_by match) resolve stale records the app's strict filter excludes — test pins to a phantom; UI never sees it. Real WI-132: getOrCreateJ04SeedLocation matched a seed with null owner_id via email-fallback; LocationContext used filter({owner_id}) and excluded the same record. Helper-app query divergence is silent until it isn't.

Toast assertions race fast API responses across all modern toast libraries (Sonner, react-hot-toast, RadixUI Toast, Mantine, Chakra, MUI Snackbar). Auto-dismiss happens at ~3-4s; assertions with 8s timeout fail when API returns in <500ms. Pattern fired 4× across Example Marketplace WI-123/127/128/132. Tests must race a short-window probe AND fall through to a durable signal (dialog close, navigation, persisted card). 3+ recurrences earns rule status.

After a failed fix, the next action MUST be reading the latest test artifact (screenshot, trace, error-context, response body) and citing a specific observation BEFORE drafting the next fix. Drafting fix-N+1 from code reading instead of evidence drives debug-by-PR loops. WI-132 prototype: 6 PRs, screenshot inspection started at PR #4, root cause visible in 1 second of looking. Cost asymmetry: ~10s evidence read vs ~90min loop.

Migrations / path-swaps proposed as fixes for an observed symptom must include probe evidence that (a) the OLD path produces the failing state, (b) the NEW path produces the passing state, against the same input. Without this proof, no-op migrations get merged: both paths produce identical end-states, symptom persists, debug-by-PR loop continues. WI-132 PR #74: helper migration to secureOperation that direct probe later showed both paths persist correctly.

'Data didn't appear in UI' bugs split cleanly into Class A (not persisted — backend) and Class B (persisted but UI doesn't see — frontend/test-infra). diagnose-bug must Phase 0 bisect via SDK probe BEFORE trace inspection. Without the bisect, debugging searches both halves of the system simultaneously, doubling effort. Probe takes 2-5min; saves 60-90min on a wrong-half search. Pattern observed in WI-097 (gte operator), WI-108→WI-113 (schema-data drift), WI-126 (user_type null), WI-132 (scope mismatch).

page.getByRole('combobox').first() and similar positional role selectors break on layout-heavy apps where chrome (sidebar language switcher, theme picker, search) renders other role-matching elements before the target. Selector strategy hierarchy: data-testid > container-scoped role > content-disambiguated role > positional .first() (last resort). WI-132 PR #75 selected the language switcher instead of location switcher; PR #77 added skip-known-language pattern.

svc has skills for WRITING E2E tests (write-e2e, playwright, e2e-automation) but no skill for ITERATING on a failing test with discipline. Each session improvises its own protocol. The 4 rules + 3 proposals filed 2026-04-27 all surfaced from a single 6-PR WI-132 session — together they reveal the meta-gap. Proposed: extend diagnose-bug with mode=e2e-test that orchestrates persistence-bisect + helper-parity + tenant-scope + transient-assertion + selector-disambiguation as mandatory phases.

For multi-entity RLS rollouts (Base44/Supabase/Firebase), DO NOT deploy highest-business-value entities first. Rank by: (1) frontend caller count ASC, (2) asServiceRole-only backend usage first, (3) exploitability — zero-caller + service-role-only entities (e.g. AuditLog, internal logging) are RLS-safe by construction and should ship first to prove the deployment mechanism. WI-115 AuditLog deploy 2026-04-28 took 30min end-to-end with zero behavior change vs picking PaymentMethod/User/Subscription first which would risk breaking customer flows.

Platform RLS engines (Base44/Supabase/Firebase) match against fields ON the entity record + user claims; they do NOT support cross-entity joins. Entities with derived ownership (Exception via Location.owner_id, Item via Location.owner_id, EmployeeBreak via Employee.user_email) cannot use the simple owner_id==user.id pattern. Three real options: (A) denormalize owner_id, (B) defense-in-depth with role check + secureOperation per-record gateway, (C) custom RPC. svc canonical pre-launch: Option B; post-launch migration to A as needed. Documented in proposal 2026-04-28-rls-derived-ownership-pattern.md.

Before deploying any access-control rule (RLS, IAM, function auth gate, header check), probe the gap as a non-privileged user. If probe fails (already blocked elsewhere), the rule may be redundant or scanner false-positive — investigate before deploying. After deploy, re-probe to confirm rule actually fires. Ship the probe as a regression E2E test. Cost asymmetry: 5-10min probe vs hours of rule-writing-then-discovering-the-gap-was-already-covered. WI-117 secrets saved 8-12h this way; WI-115 AuditLog confirmed real gap in 15min.

Base44's coding/write entities/X endpoint writes ONLY entity X's schema. Other entities' RLS rules are byte-untouched. Verified WI-115 2026-04-28: Location's WI-113 RLS rule unchanged after AuditLog deploy. This makes per-entity rollout safe — no risk of accidentally stripping prior deployments. Document as positive guarantee in Base44 CAPABILITIES.md (other platforms with global ACL files would NOT have this).

Every deployed RLS rule must ship a paired E2E regression test that probes the gap from a non-privileged client and asserts blocked. Without it, a future platform-sync overwrite (base44-builder[bot] archetype WI-066/WI-081/WI-155) silently strips the rule and no test catches it. Pattern: wi113-frontend-sdk-write-probe.critical.spec.ts (Location), wi115-rls-auditlog-regression.critical.spec.ts (AuditLog).

`until ! pgrep -f X; do sleep N; done` patterns hang forever if X never exits, leaving zombie shells the harness reports as 'running' indefinitely. Always bound: `for i in {1..30}; do pgrep -f X || break; sleep N; done; pkill -9 -f X || true`. Or use Bash run_in_background directly without the wrapper. Real session 2026-04-28 accumulated 10+ zombie until-loops that took manual pkill cleanup; the next session inherited the visual confusion.

`git worktree add` followed by `git checkout` can produce a partially-populated worktree if interrupted mid-checkout — observed twice 2026-04-28: first time entities/ directory had only 8/80 files, second time recovery via `git checkout -- entities/` failed cleanly. Workaround: after worktree creation, verify file count matches main: `(cd worktree && find . -type f | wc -l)` vs main. If mismatch, re-checkout or work directly in main with a feature branch.

Adopted 4 architectural patterns from coreyhaines/marketingskills v1.9.0 (1bcff9fc): (1) 'Before Starting' context-loading gate adapted from 1-file model to svc's 4-source chain (project-state → builder-profile → domain-profile → feature spec, read-as-needed); (2) tier-2 behavioral evals (deterministic conversation+assertions vs LLM-judge) using recorded fixtures, no live LLM calls; (3) progressive-disclosure convention (core in SKILL.md, depth in references/*.md) for new skills only — explicit non-goal: do not refactor existing skills wholesale; (4) canonical marketing context output for analyze-marketing at docs/specs/marketing-context.md with explicit no-duplication coverage matrix vs domain-profile, feature-mining-tracker, personas. The 40 marketing skills, 51+ CLIs, 52+ integration guides remain external-only via addon — coreyhaines patterns adopted as architectural improvements; the marketing skills themselves stay external because svc is not a marketing-execution framework.

Long-lived install pointers (`~/.<host>/skills/.source-repo`, hook command paths in host settings, every `~/.<host>/skills/*` symlink target) MUST have BOTH a write-time guard AND a read-time terminal fallback. Write-time guard alone (commit 52ef4eb 'setup refuses worktree' 2026-04-25) cannot retroactively repair installs already bound to ephemeral worktree paths, AND the documented `SVC_SETUP_ALLOW_WORKTREE=1` bypass keeps recreating the failure mode. WI-079, WI-080, WI-116, WI-124 each treated 'stale symlink' as the bug; the structural bug is 'install address-of-source bound to ephemeral path AND no terminal fallback in detectRepoRoot()'. WI-134 closes both layers: (a) Strategies 1+2 reject `.worktrees/` substrings, (b) Strategy 3 = filesystem scan over `~/app-workspaces` + `$SVC_REPO_SEARCH_PATHS` filtering `.worktrees/`, requiring `setup`+`hooks/svc-session-start-healthcheck.mjs`+`skills-manifest.json` to confirm canonical svc repo, with deterministic tie-break, falling through to existing warn-and-exit-0 if multiple candidates remain. Companion fix: `runSetup` timeout bumped 30s→240s — verify_commands per host can run 2-3min on cold install.

codex exec for image generation HANGS in reasoning mode if the prompt is framed as 'Generate a single abstract moodboard image: <prose description>'. It tries to plan instead of calling its generate_image tool. WORKING pattern: terse imperative — 'generate_image: <subject>, <style>, <colors>. <viewport>. Save to <path>'. Observed 41-min hang followed by clean ~90s/image when reformulated. Apply to all design-logo, generate-visuals, and landing-page invocations of codex image-gen.

Cloudflare in front of Base44 caches /public static assets (logo.svg, favicon.svg, etc.) with `cache-control: public, max-age=14400` (4 hours). After deploy, origin returns new asset but `cf-cache-status: HIT` serves stale to all visitors for up to 4hr. Diagnose with `curl -s 'https:///?cb=$RANDOM' | head` (cache-bust) vs unparametrized fetch. FIX: append `?v=N` query suffix to every / ref in source so new bundle requests fresh URLs Cloudflare hasn't cached. Bump N when asset changes. Bundle-grep verification: `curl | grep '?v=N'`.

AI alone reliably produces 6-8/10 logos, occasionally 9/10, never consistent 10/10. Remaining gap to 9-10 is human-designer work: custom typeface, taste-call asymmetry, multi-iteration glyph refinement, system extension beyond patterns. design-logo skill bakes this in via score-saturation gate (>=65/70) emitting designer-handoff brief instead of declaring victory at 56-64/70. Don't claim '10/10 every time' — promise 'production-grade ceiling + honest handoff when needed'.

Self-graded logo scoring (rubric in isolation) misses palette/context mismatches. MANDATORY before declaring logo done: render mark next to actual live page screenshots (light header AND dark hero) at correct sizes. The 4-up composite (mark vs anti-patterns vs sector refs vs in-app contexts) reveals fit problems no 7-axis rubric will catch. Saved this session: A=slate matches light page perfectly but disappears on dark hero; B=iris holds on dark but mismatches light. Solution: dual-logo system with theme-aware swap (Stripe/Linear/Notion pattern).

AI logo concepts generated from sector references alone produce sector-shaped output (rounded square + letter + dot template). Cross-domain inspiration via image-gen (architecture / Bauhaus / circadian / Dieter Rams etc.) genuinely breaks pattern-memory grooves. Verified v2 (sector-only, schedule-bar H, 4/10) vs v3 (cross-domain moodboard input, arched-doorway, 7-8/10). Skill MUST require >=3 non-sector cross-domain sources in brand-brief.yaml.

When mass-Editing ... blocks to a single-line component (e.g. ), the Edit tool can leave dangling attributes ('fetchPriority="high" />', orphan '/>' fragments) that React renders as raw text on the page. Bundle-grep, build, and isolated-component preview all PASS while the live page is broken with debug strings visible. Mitigation: after every component-swap mass edit, (1) grep for orphan attrs (loading=, fetchPriority=, width=, height=, alt= near the swapped lines), (2) run live Playwright capture in BOTH themes, (3) eyeball-check before declaring done. The 2026-04-30 Example Marketplace session shipped this exact bug to prod and only caught it on user prompt 'this skill should finish with screenshot in both light dark'.

Self-rated rubric scoring + adversarial composites + cross-model judging ALL operate on the mark in isolation. They miss: (1) palette mismatch with the actual page, (2) raw-text-leak bugs from component swap, (3) silhouette failure on the page's real background, (4) wordmark contrast failure on dark hero, (5) cached old asset serving despite new commit. The ONLY reliable terminal gate is live in-app screenshots in BOTH themes after deploy lands. Add as Phase 13 of design-logo, mandatory before declare-done. This generalizes: any skill producing a visible artifact that ships to a deployed product needs an analogous 'live in-app verification' phase as its terminal gate, not isolated-artifact scoring.

Pattern for any svc skill that produces a visual asset shipped to a live product: terminal phase MUST capture deployed evidence (Playwright live screenshot in both themes / both viewports / both auth states as relevant) and persist it to <skill-output-dir>/in-app-verification/ as the artifact future runs use as 'before' baseline. Without this, the skill self-grades isolation success while real users see the broken artifact. Generalize across design-logo, landing-page, design-ui, ad-creative, popup-cro, signup-flow-cro, paywall-upgrade-cro. Add to skill-creator template as a default phase for visual-output skills.

A monogram mark of a single letter X cannot sit next to a wordmark whose first letter is X without visual stutter. Brain reads 'X... XBrand' as duplicate, not as logo+name. Pinterest/Headspace/Mailchimp escape only because their monograms are illustrated/figurative (P-on-tomato, H-with-orange-dot, M-as-monkey). Clean geometric letterforms have no escape valve. Caught Example Marketplace session 2026-05-02 after declaring round-4 #6 H-Bauhaus winner for Example Marketplace. Add to design-logo Phase 7b as mandatory check: if monogram letter == wordmark first letter, render 4:1 lockup and disqualify on stutter.

When the founder eyeballs the 'winner' and says 'fine / okay / I guess / sure / it's something' that IS the saturation gate firing — equivalent to a hard-fail score. Skill currently treats founder enthusiasm as advisory and lets rubric score override. Wrong. Founder shrug must drop score below 60 and route back to Phase 8 with constraint escalation. Caught Example Marketplace 2026-05-02 after I declared 7-8/10 winners across 4 rounds; founder shrugged each time; skill never caught the pattern.

AI-era principle stated explicitly by framework founder: skills cannot have human-handoff exits. design-logo Phase 9b designer-handoff brief was the offending example. Plateaus are search-space problems (constraint not yet escalated), not craft-ceiling problems. The fix is constraint-escalation ladder + multi-tool refinement pipeline, not 'hire a designer'. This generalizes: any skill that produces a creative artifact and currently has a 'handoff to a human specialist' clause is broken in the AI era. Audit ALL skills for handoff phrases via lint validator. design-logo is the case study; the rule is universal.

Stored-knowledge-decay (confidence 10, 2026-04-24) generalizes to ALL classes of structured-knowledge gates, not just host capabilities. WI-140 added the SDKG primitive layer (5 files, ~150 LOC, zero npm deps) that implements the same fix mechanism (live verification + structured output + freshness validator + dedupe-aware monitoring trigger) for competitive analysis. Future framework gates (security-without-best-practice, perf-without-baseline, accessibility-without-WCAG-check, cost-without-benchmark, privacy-without-compliance-check) reuse the primitives by adding one schema + one gate config + 5-LOC validator wrappers per instance. The pattern is: schema-first (machine-readable structured data), branch-on-state-field (avoid binary block/pass — use enum like landscape_state populated|nascent|none-found|inapplicable), compensating-control framing required when domain says 'no one does this' AND project chose to do it anyway, day-1 brownfield detection invokes producer skill in scoped mode, knowledge auto-surface in research/svc-advisor when query touches registered domain. This is now the canonical svc gate pattern.

WI-140 shipped the SDKG primitive layer correctly but scoped the validator's trigger to a keyword regex (earn|redeem|verify|enroll|loyalty|points|reward). That keyword set covers ~10% of feature work. The other 90% — every non-loyalty feature — reached BASELINED with no documented industry baseline. Same selective-blindness failure mode WI-140 set out to fix, just narrowed to a different keyword set. WI-142 removed the keyword trigger: every BASELINED+ spec gets the gate (Industry Grounding section + landscape_state field), with two exemptions only — explicit landscape_inapplicable_reason frontmatter, OR Type:Enabler/Integration with UX/UI pillar [N/A — justified] (no customer-facing flow to ground). Generalizes: any structured-knowledge gate added with a keyword filter is silently incomplete. Default to universal coverage with explicit narrow exemptions, not narrow coverage with implicit broad exemptions.

Structured-knowledge gates MUST read from a structured data file at gate-time, NEVER trigger live web research. Web-fetch from a gate is slow (per-spec cost), expensive (every spec gate burns API tokens), inconsistent (intermittent failures), and re-fetches what should already be in the knowledge base. The right architecture: producer skill (analyze-competitors) populates the data file, optional async refresh (refresh-competitors, WI-143) keeps it fresh, gate reads only. WI-142 added validate-no-web-fetch-in-gate.sh as defensive lockdown — greps the engine and per-gate configs for fetch/WebSearch/curl/wget/https patterns. Generalizes to all SDKG instances: security-without-best-practice gates, accessibility-without-WCAG-check gates, etc. — all read at gate-time, refresh asynchronously.

When a structured-knowledge gate detects insufficient knowledge for the topic at hand (data file thin, missing competitor coverage, stale freshness), the gate MUST record the gap explicitly in the spec ('Note: insufficient knowledge for X; deep-dive queued as WI-XXX') and proceed with available data — NOT block the spec. Blocking on knowledge gaps inverts the framework's economic model: it makes the spec author wait synchronously for research that should run asynchronously. The gate's job is to make the gap VISIBLE in the artifact (so future readers know the basis was thin), not to gate-keep the spec lifecycle. Generalizes to any gate where the underlying data may be incomplete: prefer record-with-disclosure over hard-block.

Monogram + wordmark lockup stutter (e.g., H monogram + Example Marketplace wordmark) is a production-blocking failure that the skill did not catch. The fix is Phase 7b: render mark + wordmark side-by-side at 4:1 horizontal lockup. If the monogram letter duplicates the wordmark first character, disqualify for lockup use and loop back to Phase 3 for non-letterform alternatives. Generalizes to any mark class where the symbol and wordmark share a visual register.

When the founder says a logo is fine / okay / I guess / sure after seeing it on the live site, that is a decisive saturation failure — regardless of rubric score. The skill must loop back to Phase 8 Stage A with constraint escalation. A shrug from the person who will live with the mark is more truthful than any self-graded rubric. This generalizes to all visual-output skills: the founder eyeball is the terminal gate, not the internal score.

AI-personalized video prospecting (Sendspark / Sendr.ai / MarketBetter) reaches 15-18% reply rates steady, 25-30% on best campaigns, vs 1-2% generic text email and 8-15% hand-personalized text. Manual Loom hits 16% but caps at ~30/day; AI lipsync of prospect name + business name into a single base recording scales the same reply rate to 250+/month at the same per-prospect cost. As of 2026 this is the single largest reply-rate lever for B2B outbound and SHOULD be the default recommendation in ai-cold-outreach / cold-email / email-sequence over multichannel-text-only setups. SMB owners (cafés, restaurants, salons, single-location retailers) are visual buyers — they buy the person before the product — so video applies even more strongly than to enterprise.

Cloudflare Email Routing is INBOUND-ONLY forwarding — it does not provide outbound SMTP. Builders who set up sales1@/sales2@/etc. routing rules on Cloudflare commonly believe they have a sending setup; they do not. To send from those addresses requires either (a) Google Workspace mailbox + SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS records, (b) third-party SMTP relay (Mailgun/SendGrid/Postmark) authorized via DNS, or (c) Gmail 'Send mail as' with the destination Gmail's SMTP and proper SPF authorization (otherwise SPF/DMARC fails → spam). When a builder describes 'I send from sales1@mydomain' without naming a sending tool, the framework should explicitly verify sending mechanism + DNS authentication BEFORE recommending volume strategy. Attempting cold campaigns without proper SPF/DKIM/DMARC = automatic spam folder regardless of content quality.

For solo-founder pre-revenue outbound (€100-200/mo budget, <10k emails/month volume target), the validated 2026 cheap-stack pattern is: Smartlead Basic ($39/mo, unlimited inboxes + built-in warmup + built-in CRM) + Mailforge or LeadsMonky resold Google Workspace inboxes ($2.50-3.00/inbox vs $8.40 direct = 3.5x cost reduction) + Sendspark ($39/mo for AI video) + Apollo Free or Basic. This delivers the same architectural pattern as agency-tier stacks (EmailBison $599 + ScaledMail $199 = $798) at ~25% the cost. Lemlist ($59/mo, single-tool-do-it-all) and HubSpot CRM (free, 4-tool stack) are now both replaceable by Smartlead alone. Dedicated warmup tools (Mailwarm, Warmup Inbox) are dead in 2026 — Smartlead/Instantly bake warmup in. Recommend the cheap stack at <10k/mo; only escalate to EmailBison/ScaledMail at 100k+/mo agency-scale.

Germany (and Austria, Switzerland) operate UWG (Unfair Competition Act) ON TOP of GDPR, which enables €500-2,000 Abmahnung cease-and-desist warnings per cold-email complaint. The complainant doesn't have to be the recipient — competitors and consumer-protection associations actively monitor for cold emails to trigger Abmahnungen as a billable service. There exist German law firms whose business model is hunting cold emails. Single-prospect blasts to German lists carry asymmetric risk: 0-2% complaint rate × €500-2k = potentially €10k-40k from one campaign of 1,000 emails. Solo founders pre-revenue should EXCLUDE DE/AT/CH from cold-email blast lists and reach those prospects via LinkedIn DM only. Hand-picked 1-to-1 outreach with documented legitimate interest is far lower-risk and arguably acceptable. France/Spain/Italy/Netherlands/Portugal are 'OK with documented LIA + opt-out + sender ID + privacy link'. UK + cold-email-friendly EU east + most non-EU countries are aggressive-send territory. Critical to filter Apollo lists by country before campaign launch.

When a builder describes their existing operational setup (email infrastructure, CI/CD, hosting, payment) in shorthand and asks for strategy/budget recommendations, the framework should EXPLICITLY VERIFY the actual mechanism before sizing recommendations. Common failure mode: builder says 'I send from X@mydomain', framework assumes a real sending setup, recommends 7-domain firewall + 20-inbox strategy, then turns out the builder has only inbound forwarding and zero sending capability. Wasted: 2-3 conversation turns + a written strategy doc that needs revision. Pattern fix: when a builder names an address/tool/setup without naming the underlying mechanism, ASK ONE TARGETED CLARIFYING QUESTION upfront (e.g., 'when you press send from contact-4e517e0aab@example.invalid, what tool is the compose window in?') before recommending strategy. One question early beats three turns of revision. This is a SPECIFIC override of the question-fatigue rule for first-message setup verification — question-fatigue applies to imperative-decision contexts, NOT to first-time setup-clarification.

incidents: AP-30 recurrence 2026-05-08 via PR #75 SVC_SETUP_ALLOW_WORKTREE override
insight: When adding an override to a guard that refuses dangerous operations, the override MUST address the legitimate symptom WITHOUT re-opening the hazard the guard was protecting against. If symptom-fix and hazard-protection are mutually exclusive, the override is wrong — redesign the mechanism. Concrete: setup refused worktree invocation because symlinks would point at worktree paths. PR #75 added SVC_SETUP_ALLOW_WORKTREE=1 to unblock pre-commit hooks running from worktrees. The override let setup proceed AND keep using the worktree as symlink source — re-opening the exact hazard. Permafix: when invoked from a worktree, setup ALWAYS resolves SCRIPT_DIR to the canonical main checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, regardless of override state. Override now controls only refuse-vs-proceed, not symlink-source. Pattern check before merging any override: (a) does this override unblock a real symptom? (b) does the original refusal protection still hold post-override? (c) is there a tier-1 validator pinning (b)?

`git rm --cached <path>` on a file tracked on origin/main DELETES the file from the branch tree, producing a deletion in the PR diff. It is NOT a no-op for the PR. Correct way to remove an accidentally-staged tracked file from a PR is `git restore --source=origin/main -- <path>` then commit (restores to base, zero net diff). The wrong move was applied in PR #122 commit 6b1875a — produced a 152-line deletion that triggered a Codex HIGH finding and required a restore commit. Cost: 2 extra commits + 1 review iteration. Pattern: when removing PR noise, always confirm `git diff origin/main HEAD -- <path>` is empty after the fix.

The svc-pre-commit hook auto-stages `.svc/session-contract.jsonl` modifications into the commit being made. This means any commit during a session that has had a contract refresh ends up including local runtime state in the PR. Triggered Codex's MEDIUM finding on PR #122. Fix candidates: (a) hook excludes `.svc/session-contract.jsonl` from auto-staging, (b) move session-contract.jsonl to a path that is gitignored (e.g., `.svc/runtime/session-contract.jsonl`) and migrate consumers, (c) keep current behavior but make route-workflow strip the file from commits when on a feature branch. Option (a) is the smallest. The current state means EVERY PR authored during a working session carries session-contract noise unless the author manually unstages it.

When an author writes code intended to detect/prevent a class of failure F, the author's own code routinely reproduces F. Empirical evidence from WI-341 tranche 1: the T1 linter for the pre-WI compression gate (whose purpose is to catch product-token leakage among other things, per F-2 finding in the Codex burst review) shipped with a default behavior that auto-loaded `.svc/forbidden-tokens.example.json` as active policy — which is exactly the product-token-leakage default-behavior pattern F-2 names. Same pattern observed earlier: my proposal for the compression gate shipped with 7 findings the gate itself would have caught. This is load-bearing evidence that author-time self-review is unreliable for catching the author's own pattern reproductions. Implications: (a) cross-family adversarial review at author-time is genuinely needed (validates the discuss-phase-adversarial-review proposal), (b) the pre-WI compression gate's T1 trigger IS the right primitive — it's just not enough on its own.

Any regex matching a taxonomy value (severity rating, lane name, status, decision class, model tier) MUST be case-insensitive. Authors write taxonomy values inconsistently — 'Severity = HIGH', 'severity: high', 'Severity: High' — all should match. PR #122 T1 linter caught this minor finding: my SEVERITY_DECL_RE was `/[Ss]everity\s*[:=]\s*\**(critical|high|medium|low)\**/` — case-insensitive prefix but case-sensitive enum. Missed 'Severity = HIGH'. Fix: add `/i` flag. Generalize: every taxonomy-match regex in the framework should be reviewed for this. Candidates: validate-skill-structure (skill name casing), severity parsing in validators, lane-name matching in route-workflow, decision-class matching in plan-changeset.

When a PR is open and the user (or another agent) direct-pushes equivalent commits to main with the same content but different SHAs, the PR becomes redundant. Observed on PR #122: Claude pushed commits 7c9175e + 6b1875a + d58597e, while the user direct-pushed equivalent f4e84cd + 5b294ba to main. Net effect: origin/main has the work, but the PR branch has its own history that would conflict on rebase. The PR ends up needing to be closed-as-superseded rather than merged. Framework detection candidate: route-workflow or land-changeset should compare PR-head commit messages and content-SHAs against origin/main since the merge-base; if N commits match by content, surface a 'PR appears superseded by direct-main commits f4e84cd, 5b294ba — close?' advisory. Prevents wasted review cycles on PRs that are functionally already merged.

Tests that assert only response.success === true and field presence (URL exists, draft present, credits == 0) pass while the system silently degrades to a low-quality fallback. Example Marketplace WI-233 had a 4-content-type contract test that passed all 4 cases — every image was a 2.2 KB SVG cartoon (Groq fallback, last resort in a 5-step chain). User explicitly said goal was customer-quality images. Test caught nothing because it never looked at image.source. Fix: provider-fidelity tests MUST assert (a) source attribution is in the expected set, (b) source is NOT the cheap fallback when primary expected, (c) content quality property (mime type, file size) matches, (d) any monetary debit reconciles with source attribution. Rule landed at rules/provider-fidelity-test-contract.md.
source: Example Marketplace WI-233 → WI-238 manual pushback 2026-05-13

insight: When a provider fallback chain step has multiple post-success calls (debit wallet → write transaction → call usage-tracking), each post-success call must be wrapped in its own try/catch — NOT inside the step function's main try block. If a post-success call throws, the outer catch returns null, the chain falls through, the customer sees a different provider response, but the side-effects (wallet debit, transaction record) already executed. Result: silent money loss with mid-state damage. Example Marketplace generateAIContent had this exact bug for months — tryBase44WalletImage debited wallet -4¢ then consumeAICredit threw, response returned source=groq_svg_uploaded. Fixed in commit 35557816 by wrapping inner consumeAICredit per the pattern already used in OpenRouter/Mistral/Groq paths. Generalize: review-gate G3 should flag any provider-chain function where a side-effect call (DB write, ledger update, usage tracking) lives inside the step's main try block without inner catch.

Closing a WI by AC-checkbox satisfaction alone misses the original problem statement. Example Marketplace WI-236 closure: 6 ACs all checked, status flipped to VERIFIED. User's actual concern (stated in goal): customer-quality images. Every saved image was an SVG placeholder — the exact thing the user said not to ship. The ACs talked about persistence, schema, journey coverage; none asked about image quality. Fix: verify-promotion must re-read the WI body's "Why" / problem-statement section and confirm the evidence demonstrates resolution of THAT specific concern, not just AC-list completion. Add to verify-promotion Phase 1: "Re-read WI.md Why section. List the customer-impact properties named there. For each, point to evidence showing the property is achieved. Reject AC-only closure."

Tests against tier-gated features (paid plans, AI credits, wallet, rate limits) silently exercise whatever tier the shared test account happens to be on at run time. Example Marketplace WI-236 test account was provisioned without a Subscription → Free tier → 0 AI credits → checkAICredit refused → fallback chain landed on SVG → test passed because it only checked success flag. The test never reached the photographic path it was nominally validating. Fix: any test exercising a tier-gated feature MUST (a) declare requires_plan_tier / requires_wallet_balance / requires_credits in test metadata, (b) provision the required state in beforeAll via a fixture helper, (c) restore in afterAll if needed to not impact other tests. Pattern: e2e/helpers/ai-wallet.ts (Example Marketplace PR #14) provisions per-location wallet idempotently, isolated blast radius. Generalize across projects: any test that calls a provider whose access is gated by plan/credits/wallet state needs an ensure_X fixture in helpers/.

Journey coverage reporters and E2E run-summary scripts must use the same env-loading and account-resolution contract as the E2E runner. A reporter that checks only generic aliases such as TEST_OWNER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL can falsely mark journeys blocked even when the runner uses account pools or stream-specific aliases such as TEST_OWNER_EMAIL_STREAM_A and TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL_STREAM_A. Treat runner/reporter disagreement as a tooling bug; fix or file it before using coverage numbers as acceptance evidence.
source: Example Marketplace WI-237 coverage reporter correction, 2026-05-16

insight: For Base44 generated E2E auth accounts, SDK registration can create the account while password login remains blocked until email OTP verification. If the test domain forwards OTP email to a mailbox with an installed connector, use the connector first: resend/read OTP, call base44.auth.verifyOtp, then immediately password-login preflight. Do not add one-off Gmail OAuth refresh-token scripts while a connector can read the mailbox; custom mailbox capture belongs only in maintained harness code with ignored secrets, redacted output, and E2E-account allowlists.
source: Example Marketplace WI-304 J02 onboarding OTP unblock, 2026-05-24

insight: Corrective, regression, deploy-affecting, and acceptance-critical work must use the same selected command, journey, probe, or visual capture before and after each fix batch, then classify the delta. A broad green suite is not enough if it does not prove the exact pre/post path the user challenged. If a pre-change baseline is impossible, record no_pre_baseline_reason and replace it with old-path/new-path proof, a detached origin/main run, or an explicit blocker. Iterate fix -> same test -> compare until no acceptance-critical branch-introduced or unclassified signal remains. Machine-readable pre/post evidence should be validated with scripts/validate-pre-post-validation-evidence.mjs so command substitution, missing classifications, branch-introduced acceptance-critical signals, and multi-batch iteration records cannot false-pass as verified.
source: User correction during Example Marketplace WI-237/framework closeout, 2026-05-16

insight: When dispatching the same CI workflow filename on a different --ref than the ref your test proved success on, the workflow's `uses:` line on the target branch may pin a DIFFERENT reusable workflow than your test branch did. Same filename + same service + different branch = potentially completely different build pipeline. Failure mode: agent proves a new pipeline on a feature branch (which pins the new reusable-workflow ref); then switches to dispatching the same workflow on main to accelerate or parallelize; main's copy still pins the OLD reusable-workflow ref because the PR hasn't merged yet; the dispatches succeed (green builds) but consume the OLD pipeline. Agent reports 'N services rebuilt with property P' but the artifacts lack property P — silent regression from proven state. Mandatory pre-flight: `gh api ...contents/.github/workflows/X.yml?ref=<target-ref> | base64 -d | grep uses:` and compare to test-ref. If `@ref` differs, you're dispatching a different pipeline — either land the PR to target-ref first, keep dispatching from test-ref, or report progress under the OLD pipeline (not equivalent to test results). Companion check: post-dispatch, grep at least one build's log for dependency-resolution evidence of the expected artifact (e.g. `-SNAPSHOT` suffix presence). Green build status alone does not prove the artifact-property you expected. Generalizes to GitLab include:ref, Jenkins @Library, Buildkite plugin refs, any CI architecture where leaves pin ref to trunk-defined pipeline. Block at review-gate G7 for any fleet-rebuild closeout missing the dispatch-ref + reusable-workflow-ref pairing audit + artifact-property log evidence.

research/scripts/synthesize-meaning.mjs passes the whole input package (CAPABILITIES + all detail files) as a single gemini -p argv argument; domains whose package exceeds Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes per arg) kill the spawn with status null before gemini starts (observed twice on eic-accelerator, ~275KB package with a 212KB faq-verbatim detail file). Fix direction: write prompt to a temp file and use stdin/@file, or cap embedded detail-file bytes. Until fixed, Claude in-session synthesis is the legitimate recorded fallback (rule reason #4).

source: stripe-svc-evolve session 2026-06-07 — guard fired 2/3 for WI-364 owned by live session cd5d23fb
insight: The Stop completion guard resolve-wi fallback chain selected a WI whose claim file belongs to a DIFFERENT live session (fresh claim <15min, in-flight uncommitted GREEN-phase work in the WI worktree) and emitted hard execute-pressure at a session that never claimed it. Resolution steps active-WI-claim-file and single-in_progress-graph must verify claim session id == current session OR claim staleness past TTL before treating the WI as this session contract; a foreign fresh claim must downgrade the guard to advisory/skip. Failure mode prevented: a second orchestrator obeying the guard dual-claims the WI, executes tasks in a worktree mid-edit by the owner session, and corrupts both sessions state — the exact crosstalk WI-352 claim files were added to prevent, bypassed because the guard reads the claim file for WI-name resolution but not for ownership. Pre-action check that caught it: read .svc/claims/<WI>.claim.json session field + worktree mtime/git status BEFORE obeying cross-WI completion pressure. Companion hazard from the same session: a persisted shell cd into the foreign worktree silently redirected relative-path file writes into the other session checkout — always use absolute paths or git -C when a foreign worktree exists.

Any multi-KB prompt package to a CLI harness (codex exec, gemini -p) must go via stdin or @file, never argv — Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072/arg) kills the spawn with Argument list too long / status null. Second observed class member (synthesize-meaning.mjs was first). codex exec accepts - for stdin.

Cross-model review packages and file-set parity checks on a long-lived worktree branch MUST use three-dot (merge-base) diff, not two-dot. Parallel-orchestrator commits on main otherwise appear as foreign reversals: 400KB package vs 60KB real changeset at WI-364 G6; two-dot file-set check false-flagged 20 foreign knowledge files.

Adopting codegen over hand-maintained doc sections: (1) write renders that reproduce CURRENT content byte-identically (variant params for shape differences; desc-merge for hand-curated prose), (2) insert ONLY marker lines (numstat +N/-0, zero non-marker added lines), (3) require --check == fresh BEFORE first --write, (4) prove idempotency (write x2 byte-identical). Catches blueprint/reality drift (plain-bullets vs descriptions, 3-col vs 4-col tables) before any content is destroyed.

insight: git notes are per-SHA: rebasing a commit (even tree-identical) orphans its tree-bound quick-fix/envelope note on the pre-rebase SHA and the push gate refuses the new SHA. After any rebase of noted commits, re-emit the note for the new SHA (tree unchanged = mechanically re-verifiable) or notes-copy old->new before pushing.

NEVER write ~/.claude/settings.json keys from remembered/derived shapes — skillOverrides takes STRING enums (on|name-only|user-invocable-only|off), not {nameOnly:true} objects; the wrong shape made Claude refuse settings load in EVERY other folder (live user-facing regression, caught by user not by any gate). Before mutating host config: verify the exact schema against live docs or an existing valid entry, write, then VALIDATE by parsing AND launching/dry-running the host check if available. Machine-local edits bypass all repo gates — the backup+restore line is necessary but not sufficient.

When dieting a SKILL.md (or any doc) into mandate-line + reference pointer, the compressed mandate MUST be derived by quoting/condensing the just-extracted text — NEVER written from memory of what the section says. WI-366 G6 caught: G0 scope modes written from recall as full/trim/phase while the verbatim-moved protocol says Expand/Selective-Expand/Hold/Reduce; worse, the freshly-authored comprehension prompt encoded the same hallucination, so the 6/6 gate validated the regression. Same class: pointer targets (§Phase receipts) referenced sections that were never appended. Method: extract first, re-read the extraction, THEN write the summary + pointers, and author/verify gate prompts against the extraction, not memory.

analyze-marketing (and any spec-mining skill) structurally cannot detect ABSENCE: a refresh passed no-loss + self-verify yet missed ~12 live sellable capabilities (voice+AI-image creation, arrival push, standby queues, events, inbox/broadcasts, perks passport) because (1) capability truth lived in pages/function-slugs/feature-flags with stale-or-missing specs, (2) depth-first 3-4-spec batching never builds a breadth denominator, (3) all self-verify checks test presence/correctness of what IS written, never what ISN'T. meta_pattern: Author re-reading own output verifies correctness, never absence — absence detection requires an independent blind reader over a mechanically-built surface denominator. Applies to any extraction/inventory skill (marketing context, capability registry, coverage audits).
